summary: The new diagnostic-set comparison addresses the count-replacement case, but the pipeline can hide a TypeScript invocation failure. The source-change fallback also lacks a concrete comparison command.
blocking_findings: F1 [Blocker] spec D6 and plan tasks 1.1 and 3.1: The diagnostic identity comparison still can pass without a usable TypeScript result. Rationale: The pipeline ends with sort, so it returns success even when tsc fails before emitting file-and-position diagnostics; grep drops such output and creates an empty set, which passes comm -13. This can occur if an updated compiler rejects an option or emits a fatal diagnostic without a source location. Preserve and validate the tsc exit status and reject unparsed errors before comparing sets.
nonblocking_findings: F2 [Major] spec D6 and plan tasks 1.1 and 3.1: Define the comparison command for the source-change fallback. Rationale: The spec says to drop line and column and retain file, code, and message text when Green names a source change, but gives no extraction or comparison command for that case. Since the plan permits a named source change when a major bump forces one, this leaves an edge-case gate for the implementer to design.

paraphrase.proposes: This track refreshes harness dependencies, clears critical and high advisories, and records reasons for residual advisories. It keeps fixture dependencies pinned for benchmark comparability. It compares post-refresh type-check diagnostics with the base set and runs compatibility checks for Playwright changes.
paraphrase.current_system: The harness has no tsconfig or type-check script. The base type-check produces 210 diagnostics. The TypeScript command emits source-location diagnostics and multi-line explanatory text. The Playwright configuration uses system Chrome, and scoring pins react-doctor 0.9.2.

git diff --name-only a64e681..HEAD lists only measure/tracks/deps_refresh/spec.md, plan.md, and spec-review.md.
The base diagnostic file has 210 sorted entries. Its identities use the actual TypeScript form `file(line,col): error TScode`.

The grep pattern matches the primary diagnostic line. Its `^[^(]+` prefix accepts spaces in the file path up to the opening parenthesis. Continuation lines do not match and are not needed for the specified location-and-code identity.

F1 remains: tsc output is piped through grep and sort without preserving the tsc exit status or rejecting unmatched fatal output. A missing executable or an unlocated compiler error can produce an empty after-set, and the subset comparison then passes.
F2: the source-change branch changes identity fields but gives no command or precise serialization for that branch.
